name: Googie
fit: Hospitality, local business, optimistic startups, events
keywords: atomic age roadside diner mid-century sign neon
idea: Atomic-age roadside modernism. Starbursts, boomerangs and orbiting atoms in mustard, teal and coral, and a motel sign with chasing bulbs that lights up at dusk.
note: Live: the bulbs chase and the atom orbits on their own. "Light the sign" turns day into dusk: the sky goes navy and the neon VACANCY tube and sparkles glow.
borrowed: 1950s–60s Googie architecture and roadside Americana: coffee-shop roofs, motel signs with chaser bulbs and neon "Vacancy" tubes, starbursts, boomerang laminate patterns, Sputnik chandeliers and atomic orbit logos.
mood: Optimistic, friendly, a little kitsch. Suits hospitality, local businesses, events, consumer apps and startups that want "the future is fun" instead of "the future is grey". The day/dusk switch makes a natural light/dark theme.

type.meta: Labels & body · Josefin Sans 400/700, caps tracked +0.24em

patterns.label: Boomerang laminate

motion: Bulbs: two radial-gradient layers (lit/unlit) shifted half a period with `steps(2)`, so the light chases; faster at dusk.
Starburst turns once a minute; the atom's electrons ride SVG `animateMotion` paths.
Day → dusk: one class swaps the sky token and switches the neon on with layered `text-shadow`, over 600–800ms.
watchouts: Shrikhand is a sign face: headlines and logos only, never paragraphs.
Coral on cream sits near 3:1. Use it for large display type only; body text stays ink.
Kitsch overload is easy. Keep the decoration to the hero and let the rest breathe on cream.
